abstract: BACKGROUND: Testicular cancer is the most common solid cancer diagnosed among young men. Despite good response to chemotherapy and a high survival rate, subsequent salvage therapies may still be required for some patients in advanced stages. The predictive and prognostic markers are crucial unmet needs. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed advanced testicular cancer patients who had received first-line chemotherapy between January 2002 and December 2020. The associations between baseline characteristics and clinical outcomes were evaluated. RESULTS: Of the 68 included patients, the median age was 29 years. Among them, 40 patients received only first-line chemotherapy while the remaining 28 received subsequent chemotherapy or surgeries. Data reveal that 82.5% (33/40) of the patients in the chemotherapy-only group were recorded as a good prognostic risk using the International Germ Cell Cancer Collaborative Group classification when compared with 35.7% (10/28) in the second-line therapy group. In the chemotherapy-only group, 53.8% of patients were presented with lymph node metastasis compared with 78.6% in the second-line therapy group ( p = 0.068). Fifteen percent of patients (6/40) were recorded as S stage 2-3 in the chemotherapy-only group, whereas 85.2% (23/28) were recorded as such in the second-line therapy group ( p < 0.001). The 5-year overall survival estimation was 92.9% in the chemotherapy-only group and 77.3% in the second-line therapy group. Univariate analysis for overall survival revealed that those patients at the S 2-3 stage and those receiving second-line therapies showed a trend of having an increased death risk (hazard ratio [HR] = 8.26, 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.99-68.67, p = 0.051; HR = 7.76, 95% CI, 0.93-64.99, p = 0.059, respectively). The S 2-3 stage was also independently associated with the risk of subsequent therapy (HR = 33.13; 95% CI, 2.55-430.64, p = 0.007). CONCLUSION: Our real-world data show the predictive role of serum tumor marker stage 2-3 to be associated with any subsequent therapies after first-line chemotherapy. This can facilitate clinical decision making during the testicular cancer treatment process.
abstract_ja: 背景：精巣がんは若年男性で最も多く診断される固形がんである。化学療法への良好な反応と高い生存率にもかかわらず、進行期の一部の患者では後続のサルベージ治療が必要となることがある。予測因子および予後因子は重要な未充足ニーズである。方法：2002年1月から2020年12月の間に一次化学療法を受けた進行精巣がん患者を後方視的に解析した。ベースライン特性と臨床転帰との関連を評価した。結果：対象となった68例の患者の年齢中央値は29歳であった。そのうち40例は一次化学療法のみを受け、残りの28例は後続の化学療法または手術を受けた。国際胚細胞がん共同研究グループの分類を用いると、化学療法のみの群の82.5%(33/40)が良好な予後リスクと記録されたのに対し、二次治療群では35.7%(10/28)であった。化学療法のみの群では53.8%の患者にリンパ節転移が認められ、二次治療群では78.6%であった(p = 0.068)。化学療法のみの群では、40例中6例(15%)がS病期2～3と記録されたのに対し、二次治療群では28例中23例(85.2%)がそのように記録された(p < 0.001)。全生存期間について単変量解析を行ったところ、S病期2～3の患者および二次治療を受けた患者は、死亡リスクが高くなる傾向が認められた(ハザード比[HR] = 8.26、95%信頼区間(CI) 0.99～68.67、p = 0.051；HR = 7.76、95% CI 0.93～64.99、p = 0.059)。S病期2～3は、後続治療のリスクとも独立して関連していた(HR = 33.13；95% CI 2.55～430.64、p = 0.007)。結論：本実臨床データは、血清腫瘍マーカーによるS病期2～3が、一次化学療法後の後続治療の必要性と関連するという予測的役割を示している。これは精巣がんの治療過程における臨床的意思決定を支援しうる。
